title: Iranian Cargo Vessel Struck Off Qeshm Island, One Killed, Hours Before Iran-Gulf Hormuz Talks
detail: An Iranian commercial cargo vessel was struck early Sunday roughly 14 miles from Bandar Abbas, off Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, killing one of its 10 crew members and wounding four others, Iran's state-run IRNA news agency reported. The Qeshm governor blamed a 'terrorist enemy' for the strike; the projectile's origin was not immediately identified, and there was no immediate comment from the US military, which has struck Iranian-flagged vessels during its blockade of Iranian ports. The attack came one day before Iran was set to brief Gulf Cooperation Council counterparts and Iraq in Salalah, Oman on its contested efforts to manage strait shipping; only Iraq had publicly confirmed attendance, while Bahrain declined, citing the absence of diplomatic relations with Tehran. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian responded: 'Our people can't be bullied into submission. Iran won't surrender.' President Trump, speaking from his golf course in Doonbeg, Ireland, said Iran 'wants to make a deal so bad' and is 'calling constantly.'

media.caption: An Iranian cargo vessel is struck off Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, killing one crew member, a day before planned Iran-Gulf talks in Oman

title: Houthis Complete Takeover of Yemen's Red Sea Coastline, Now Control Both Bab el-Mandeb Shipping Lanes
detail: Iran-backed Houthi forces completed their rapid seizure of Yemen's Red Sea coastline over the weekend of Sep 11-13, capturing the strategic island of Mayyun (Perim) -- which splits Bab el-Mandeb into its two shipping lanes and fell Sep 11 -- along with the Greater and Lesser Hanish islands, after already taking the port city of Mokha on Sep 10. The group is now positioned roughly 20km (12 miles) from the African coast and effectively controls the strait, through which about 12% of global trade, 11% of seaborne oil and 8% of LNG normally passes. Al Jazeera reported Red Sea nations watching closely as the Houthis' grip tightens alongside the still-closed Strait of Hormuz and Saudi Arabia's shuttered East-West pipeline -- three chokepoints under strain simultaneously. A Houthi official claimed 'freedom of navigation and international trade in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandeb are safe and orderly,' though shipping companies remained cautious given an earlier Houthi statement that navigation would be safe 'for all companies except for Saudi vessels.' More than 2,000 Yemenis fled to Djibouti within 24 hours of the advance, straining humanitarian resources in the region.

media.caption: Houthi forces complete their takeover of Yemen's Red Sea coastline, gaining control of both Bab el-Mandeb shipping lanes
